slot.subtopic: Work done by friction on incline
slot.brief: A block released from rest slides down a long rough incline of known incline angle and friction coefficient; find fraction of initial energy lost to heat, using work-energy theorem with friction.

stem: A $2.0\ \text{kg}$ block slides from rest down a rough incline through a vertical drop of $15\ \text{m}$. For $\theta=37^\circ$, $\mu=0.30$, $\sin37^\circ=0.60$, $\cos37^\circ=0.80$ and $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, what percentage of its initial gravitational potential energy is dissipated by friction?

verdicts.working: The distance along the incline is s = h/sinθ. The frictional-energy fraction is μmg cosθ · s/(mgh) = μ cotθ = 0.30(0.80/0.60) = 0.40.

working:
$s=15/0.60=25\ \text{m}$; $W_f=\mu mg\cos\theta\,s=0.30(2)(10)(0.80)(25)=120\ \text{J}$; $mgh=300\ \text{J}$; $100W_f/(mgh)=40\%$.

Independent check: The distance along the incline is s = h/sinθ. The frictional-energy fraction is μmg cosθ · s/(mgh) = μ cotθ = 0.30(0.80/0.60) = 0.40.
solution:
The distance travelled along the incline is $s=\frac{h}{\sin\theta}=\frac{15}{0.60}=25\ \text{m}$. The work done by friction is
$$W_f=\mu mg\cos\theta\,s=0.30(2)(10)(0.80)(25)=120\ \text{J}.$$The initial potential energy is $mgh=300\ \text{J}$, so the dissipated percentage is $\frac{120}{300}\times100=40\%$.
